resources.string: Reports arrive/leave to your own hub. Nothing else, nobody else.

Pair the app on your phone first
Location: foreground only — a geofence needs \"Allow all the time\"
Home: not set — pair to fetch it from the hub
Device id: %1$s\nUse this as the token\'s device id on the hub so you can revoke this phone alone.

Android will ask again, and this time you must choose "Allow all the time".

Without it, the geofence stops the moment you close the app — which is exactly when you need it (arriving home with your phone in your pocket).

This app only sends your position to your own hub, and only when you cross your home boundary.

Drive mode starts when your car's Bluetooth connects, which also happens when you're sat in the car going nowhere — and it keeps recording while you walk away from a parked car.

Allowing this lets the app tell driving from walking, so a journey is the drive and nothing else.

It is used on your phone only, and is never sent anywhere but your own hub.
Physical activity denied — journeys will still record, but may include time parked or on foot.
Android won\'t ask again from inside the app. To enable it: Settings → Permissions → Location → Allow all the time.
Battery: optimised — Android may delay reports for hours between app opens
Battery: unrestricted — reports run on schedule

Android delays background work more the less often an app is opened — exactly when you are away from home and presence matters most. Left this way, reports can slip from every 15–60 minutes to once every few hours, and the hub will show you as \"unknown\" in between.\n\nAllowing background use only lifts that throttling. This app still does nothing continuously — it reports on the same schedule either way, just without the delay.
Could not open the background-use prompt. Enable it manually: Settings → Apps → ZMM Presence → Battery → Unrestricted.
